_what_this_is: Measured thresholds for the five-voter semantic ensemble (WORDS-A constraint 3). Every value here is the midpoint of a measured gap between the closest true case and the closest false one, recorded with that margin. A voter with no entry has NO MEASURABLE THRESHOLD on that decision and does not vote; the ensemble then refuses, by constraint 4, rather than proceeding with fewer than five.
_measurement: docs/fix/ENSEMBLE_THRESHOLDS.md carries the full method and result. Leave-one-out over the operator's reference set plus all 44 shipped convention rules as true negatives.
_do_not_round: These are not round numbers and must not be rounded. Each sits at the midpoint of a measured gap. A number chosen so that a voter can participate is exactly what constraint 3 forbids.

redaction_intent._measured_on: 15 positive references, 12 negative references, 44 shipped convention rules as additional true negatives
redaction_intent._result: ONE voter of five separates the classes. Four overlap: their closest true case scores BELOW their closest false case, so no threshold separates them and none is invented here.
redaction_intent._consequence: The ensemble REFUSES this decision under constraint 4 and names the four voters lacking a measured threshold. That is the designed behaviour of a rule that cannot be satisfied on the data available, and it is the operator's to resolve, not mine. See ENSEMBLE_THRESHOLDS.md for what would make five voters possible; the short answer is a larger and lexically varied reference set, which is operator-written text.

_sbert_margin.note: separates cleanly; threshold is the midpoint of the gap
